g=9.8 \, \mathrm{N/kg} & G=6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \mathrm{N \cdot m^{2}/kg^{2}} \\

N_{\mathrm{A}}=6.02 \times 10^{23} \, \mathrm{mol^{-1}} & R=N_{\mathrm{A}} k_{\mathrm{B}}=8.31 \, \mathrm{J/(mol \cdot K)} \\
\sigma=5.67 \times 10^{-8} \, \mathrm{J/(s \cdot m^{2} \cdot K^{4})} & e=1.602 \times 10^{-19} \, \mathrm{C} \\

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The problem gives the potential at the center of a uniformly charged cube of side length L as Φ_center(L) ≈ 0.1894 ρ L²/ε₀. To find the potential at a corner of one cube of side a, place 8 identical cubes of side a so that they all meet at that corner. These 8 cubes form a larger cube of side 2a, and the shared corner becomes the center of the larger cube. By symmetry, each of the 8 smaller cubes contributes the same potential at that central point. Therefore, 8 Φ_corner(a) = Φ_center(2a). Substituting L = 2a gives Φ_center(2a) ≈ 0.1894 ρ (2a)²/ε₀ = 0.1894 · 4 ρ a²/ε₀. Thus Φ_corner(a) = [0.1894 · 4 / 8] ρ a²/ε₀ = 0.0947 ρ a²/ε₀.

method.method_draft: Compute the corner potential directly from Coulomb’s potential integral. Read from the text that the cube has uniform density ρ and side length a, and place the origin at the chosen corner with the cube occupying 0≤x,y,z≤a. Then Φ_corner=(ρ/(4πε0))∫_0^a∫_0^a∫_0^a dx dy dz / sqrt(x^2+y^2+z^2). Substitute x=au, y=av, z=aw to factor out a^2: Φ_corner=(ρa^2/ε0) C, where C=(1/(4π))∫_0^1∫_0^1∫_0^1 du dv dw / sqrt(u^2+v^2+w^2). Evaluate this dimensionless integral numerically, or by using the known closed-form logarithm/arctangent antiderivative, to obtain C≈0.0947.
method.CoT_raw: Place the origin at the chosen corner of the uniformly charged cube. Then the cube occupies 0 ≤ x,y,z ≤ a, and the electric potential at the corner is the Coulomb potential integral over the cube: Φ_corner = (ρ/(4πε0)) ∫_0^a ∫_0^a ∫_0^a dx dy dz / sqrt(x^2 + y^2 + z^2). The singularity at the corner is integrable. Now scale variables by x = au, y = av, z = aw. Then dx dy dz = a^3 du dv dw and sqrt(x^2+y^2+z^2)=a sqrt(u^2+v^2+w^2), so the integral factors as a^2 times a dimensionless integral. Thus Φ_corner = (ρ a^2/ε0) C, where C = (1/(4π)) ∫_0^1 ∫_0^1 ∫_0^1 du dv dw / sqrt(u^2+v^2+w^2). Numerically, this dimensionless integral is approximately 1.19007, giving C ≈ 1.19007/(4π) ≈ 0.0947. This is also half of the given center coefficient 0.1894, consistent with decomposing the centered cube into eight corner subcubes.
